description:
The unreleased changelog describes the release it will ship, so no entry names a route this release does not have.

## Background

The unreleased section accumulated entries across a container that changed the same subject twice. Several were written while the binary still carried a compiled-in package and describe it as a live resolution route: one names it as an answering step in dependency resolution, one says a package directory lets an adopter avoid consulting it, and three describe an origin, a stored-record failure case, and a compile-time read route that distinguish compiled-in bytes from directory bytes. That distinction no longer exists.

The change that removed it has no entry at all, so the section simultaneously describes a route the release does not have and omits the removal that took it away. Both halves are one defect: an unreleased entry is not history, it is a draft of what the release will say, and an adopter reading it would be told about something no release ever carried.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: No unreleased entry describes the binary as carrying, resolving from, or falling back to a compiled-in profile package or workflow preset.
- [hard] REQ-02: The removal of the compiled-in package and the workflow presets is recorded as an unreleased entry, in the register the surrounding entries use.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every unreleased entry that survives is true of the tree at this revision, and each still reads as one coherent statement rather than a patched one.
title: Reconcile the unreleased changelog against the release it describes
